## Design

### 2026-10-09 – half life session 1 writeup: the pendant (10.75 hrs)

**10.75h**

half life session 1 writeup: the pendant (10.75 hrs)

intro

hey!! so this is my first ever half life session and i'm honestly so excited to be writing this. a bit of background: i've been wanting to build a wearable that records conversations for a long time, like a little pendant that remembers everything people say so you never lose a good idea, a meeting detail, or some random thing a friend told you. i finally sat down, started the timer, and ended up going for 10.75 hours straight. by the end i'd designed the first half of the whole design, and i'm way more hyped than when i started.

the one rule i set for myself before anything else: it has to be private by design. a thing that records people is only ok if everyone around you can trust it. so basically every decision below came back to that.

the brain: microcontroller

i went with an ESP32-S3* (probably a XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense*, because its tiny and already has a mic and sd card slot on it). reasons: it has wifi + bluetooth built in, enough power to run voice detection on-device, it sips power in deep sleep, and its small enough to actually fit in a pendant. i looked at the nRF52840 too since its crazy good on battery, but the esp32 has way more ram and wifi, which i need for uploading audio.

the mic

a MEMS I2S microphone* (like the INMP441 or the SPH0645*). digital audio straight into the esp32 over I2S, no noisy analog stuff to deal with. i picked this because the audio is cleaner and the whole thing is tiny.

the privacy button

this was my favorite thing to design. i'm using a physical slide switch* (not a push button) that cuts the power line to the mic itself. so when its off, its actually off. its not the software going "ok i promise i stopped". a slide switch is better than a push button here because you can see/feel which position it's in without looking at anything. next to it theres a status led* that glows when recording is on, so people near you can see it too. i also planned a second tiny push button* for stuff like marking a "this part is important" moment, double tap to bookmark a conversation, etc.

voice detection (VAD)

the pendant doesn't record 24/7. it idles, and a voice activity detection step decides when someone is actually talking. i'm planning to use Silero VAD* or the lighter WebRTC VAD* on the esp32. it only starts capturing when it hears speech, and keeps a small pre-roll buffer (like 1-2 seconds) so it doesn't chop off the first word. there's also a hangover time, so it waits a couple seconds of silence before stopping and doesn't cut people off mid sentence. saves battery and storage a lot.

storage

two layers. first, audio gets saved on the device in chunks to a microSD card* so nothing is lost if theres no wifi. then when it connects, chunks get uploaded in the background and deleted from the card after the server confirms it. for the cloud side i'm thinking Supabase* (postgres + file storage + auth in one place). each recording gets a row with a timestamp, duration, transcript, summary, tags, and a link to the audio file. i also planned a retry queue so a dropped connection doesn't mean lost audio.

the AI pipeline + AI router

this is where it gets fun. the flow is: audio uploaded, then speech to text, then summary + action items + topics, then saved to the database and made searchable.

transcription: Whisper* (either the api or a self hosted faster-whisper) or Deepgram* if i want speaker labels
summaries/search: an LLM, like Claude*
AI router: instead of hardcoding one model, i'm putting a router in front of everything (something like OpenRouter* or my own small router layer). it sends short/simple stuff (quick summaries, tagging) to a cheaper, faster model and only sends the long or complicated conversations to a stronger one. that keeps costs low and gives me fallbacks if one provider goes down.
search: embeddings stored with pgvector* so you can ask stuff like "what did we decide about the budget" and it finds the right moment

where i'm at

so thats the first half of the design done: the privacy switch, the mic and microcontroller choice, voice detection, storage, and the whole AI pipeline with the router. 5.5 hours felt like nothing, which is always how you know a project is good.
